_doc: Major temples by deity, for the Temples screen. 'site' and 'donate' are only ever a temple's own official address, checked on 2026-10-21 and, for the temples in Nepal and the United States, 2026-10-22 (government .gov.in/.nic.in portals, the temple board's own domain, or a domain the temple's Wikipedia entry and official notices name). Several look-alike domains were found serving spam, so nothing is added from a guess: a temple whose official address could not be confirmed has neither, and the app says offerings are made at the temple; one whose site has no donation page of its own has the site only. Descriptions say why a temple is significant and famous; no remedies, papam or fear framing (content/scripts/audit_content.py). English for now; native text to follow with review.

temples.name: Sri Venkateswara Swamy Temple
temples.about: On the seventh of the Tirumala hills stands Lord Venkateswara, Vishnu as he came to dwell in the Kali Yuga. It is among the most visited places of worship in the world, famous for its laddu prasadam, for devotees offering their hair in gratitude, and for the Brahmotsavam each autumn.

temples.name: Guruvayur Sri Krishna Temple
temples.about: Guruvayurappan, Krishna as a child holding the conch, discus, mace and lotus, is said to have been installed by Guru and Vayu, which gives the town its name. Called the Dwaraka of the South, it is famous for its many first-rice ceremonies and weddings, its temple elephants, and the Guruvayur Ekadasi.

temples.name: Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple
temples.about: Vishnu reclines on the serpent Ananta in an image so large it is seen through three doors: the face, the navel with Brahma on the lotus, and the feet. One of the 108 Divya Desams, it gave Thiruvananthapuram its name and is known for its Dravidian gopuram and its Alpashy and Painkuni festivals.

temples.name: Badrinath Temple
temples.about: High in the Garhwal Himalaya beside the Alaknanda, Badrinarayan is Vishnu in meditation. One of the four Char Dham and among the 108 Divya Desams, it is open from spring to the onset of winter, when the deity is taken down to Joshimath.

temples.name: Shri Vitthal Rukmini Mandir
temples.about: Vitthal, Krishna standing on a brick with hands on his hips, waiting for his devotee Pundalik, is the heart of Maharashtra's Varkari tradition. Every Ashadhi Ekadashi the wari, lakhs of pilgrims walking from Alandi and Dehu singing the abhangas of Dnyaneshwar and Tukaram, arrives here.

temples.name: Shree Jagannath Temple
temples.about: Jagannath, Lord of the Universe, with Balabhadra and Subhadra, is worshipped in wooden forms renewed in the Nabakalebara ceremony. One of the Char Dham, it is famous for the Rath Yatra, when the three ride out on giant chariots, and for the Mahaprasad cooked in its vast kitchen.

temples.name: Sri Ranganathaswamy Temple
temples.about: On an island in the Kaveri, Ranganatha reclines on Adisesha. The first of the 108 Divya Desams and among the largest functioning temple complexes in the world, with seven enclosures and the towering Rajagopuram, it celebrates Vaikunta Ekadasi on a grand scale.

temples.name: Shri Kashi Vishwanath Temple
temples.about: Vishwanath, Lord of the Universe, is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas, on the western bank of the Ganga in Kashi, held to be among the oldest living cities. The gilded spire and the Kashi Vishwanath Dham corridor down to the ghats draw pilgrims all year, above all on Maha Shivaratri and in Shravan.

temples.name: Shree Somnath Jyotirlinga
temples.about: Counted first among the twelve Jyotirlingas, Somnath stands on the Saurashtra coast where the Moon is said to have worshipped Shiva. Rebuilt many times through its history and restored in 1951, it is known for its sea-facing setting and evening light and sound show.

temples.name: Shri Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga
temples.about: The south-facing Jyotirlinga of Mahakal, Shiva as lord of time, stands in the ancient city of Ujjain. It is famous for the Bhasma Aarti before dawn and for the Simhastha Kumbh Mela held on the Shipra every twelve years.

temples.name: Kedarnath Temple
temples.about: The highest of the Jyotirlingas, Kedarnath stands at the head of the Mandakini valley, reached on foot from Gaurikund. One of the Char Dham and the Panch Kedar, its stone temple has withstood centuries of Himalayan winters; it opens in spring and closes after Diwali.

temples.name: Sri Bhramaramba Mallikarjuna Swamy Temple
temples.about: In the Nallamala hills above the Krishna, Mallikarjuna is both a Jyotirlinga and, with Goddess Bhramaramba, one of the Shakti Peethas, a rare meeting of the two. It is known for its fortified walls carved with scenes from the epics and for its Maha Shivaratri Brahmotsavam.

temples.name: Shri Trimbakeshwar Jyotirlinga
temples.about: Near the source of the Godavari in the Brahmagiri hills, Trimbakeshwar's Jyotirlinga has three small faces representing Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva. Its black-stone temple was built in the eighteenth century, and Nashik-Trimbak hosts the Kumbh Mela every twelve years.

temples.name: Arulmigu Ramanathaswamy Temple
temples.about: On Pamban island, Ramanathaswamy is the Jyotirlinga where Rama is said to have worshipped Shiva before crossing to Lanka. One of the Char Dham, it is famous for the longest temple corridors in India and for the 22 theerthams, wells in which pilgrims bathe.

temples.name: Shri Mata Vaishno Devi
temples.about: In a cave on the Trikuta hills the Goddess is worshipped as three natural rock forms, the pindis of Mahakali, Mahalakshmi and Mahasaraswati. Millions make the twelve-kilometre climb from Katra each year, many through the night, calling 'Jai Mata Di'.

temples.name: Maa Kamakhya Temple
temples.about: On Nilachal hill above the Brahmaputra, Kamakhya is among the most revered of the Shakti Peethas, where the Goddess is worshipped without an image, in a natural stone yoni within the sanctum. It is the centre of the Shakta tradition and famous for the Ambubachi Mela each June.

temples.name: Arulmigu Meenakshi Sundareswarar Temple
temples.about: Meenakshi, the fish-eyed Goddess and queen of Madurai, with Sundareswarar, Shiva, stands at the centre of the city. Its fourteen gopurams covered in painted figures, the Hall of a Thousand Pillars and the Chithirai festival, re-enacting their celestial wedding, make it one of Tamil Nadu's great temples.

temples.name: Attukal Bhagavathy Temple
temples.about: Attukal Amma, identified with Kannaki of the Silappatikaram, is worshipped as a mother who protects. The Attukal Pongala each Kumbham sees lakhs of women cook pongala in the open across the city, recorded as one of the largest gatherings of women in the world.

temples.name: Sri Durga Malleswara Swamy Varla Devasthanam
temples.about: On Indrakeeladri hill above the Krishna, Kanaka Durga is believed to have appeared on her own. The Dasara Navaratri here, with the Goddess adorned in a different alankaram each day and the Teppotsavam on the river, is among the biggest in the Telugu states.

temples.name: Shri Mahalaxmi (Ambabai) Temple
temples.about: Ambabai, Mahalakshmi of Kolhapur, is one of the Shakti Peethas and the presiding goddess of the city. The temple is known for the Kiranotsav, days in the year when the setting sun's rays reach the deity's face, and for its Navaratri.

temples.name: Sri Sharadamba Temple, Sringeri
temples.about: On the Tunga river, Sharadamba, Saraswati, presides over the first of the maths founded by Adi Shankaracharya. Families come for Aksharabhyasa, a child's first letters, especially at Navaratri, and the Vidyashankara temple's zodiac pillars catch the sun month by month.

temples.name: Shree Siddhivinayak Ganapati Mandir
temples.about: Siddhivinayak, a right-trunked Ganapati with Riddhi and Siddhi, has been worshipped at Prabhadevi since 1801. Mumbai's best-loved temple, it draws long queues on Tuesdays and on Angarki Sankashti Chaturthi, and from people of every walk of life before a new beginning.

temples.name: Shrimant Dagdusheth Halwai Ganpati
temples.about: Founded in the 1890s by the sweet-maker Dagdusheth Gadve, this Ganapati is at the centre of Pune's Ganeshotsav, the public festival Lokmanya Tilak popularised. Its richly adorned idol, themed pandals and the trust's social work are known across Maharashtra.

temples.name: Sri Varasiddhi Vinayaka Swamy Temple
temples.about: The self-manifested Vinayaka of Kanipakam is said to have emerged from a well and to keep growing. Rebuilt by the Chola king Kulothunga I, the temple is known for its Brahmotsavam beginning on Vinayaka Chavithi and for promises made before the deity.

temples.name: Karpaga Vinayagar Temple
temples.about: A rock-cut Karpaga Vinayagar with two arms and a right-curving trunk, carved in the cave temple by early Pandya craftsmen, is among the oldest images of Ganesha in Tamil Nadu. The ten-day Vinayagar Chathurthi festival ends with a giant modakam offered to him.

temples.name: Arulmigu Dhandayuthapani Swamy Temple
temples.about: On a hill above Palani, Murugan stands as Dhandayuthapani, the renunciant with a staff, in an image said to be made of navapashanam by the siddha Bogar. One of the six Arupadai Veedu, it is famous for the panchamritam prasadam and for Thai Poosam, when pilgrims walk from far away carrying kavadi.

temples.name: Arulmigu Subramaniya Swamy Temple
temples.about: The only one of the six Arupadai Veedu by the sea, Tiruchendur is where Murugan is said to have overcome Surapadman. The Kandha Sashti festival culminating in the Soorasamharam on the shore draws great crowds each year.

temples.name: Kukke Shree Subrahmanya Temple
temples.about: In the forests of the Western Ghats beside the Kumaradhara, Subrahmanya is worshipped as lord of the serpents, with Vasuki. The temple is known for its Champa Shashti festival in Margashira and as one of the most visited temples in Karnataka.

temples.name: Arulmigu Swaminatha Swamy Temple
temples.about: One of the six Arupadai Veedu, Swamimalai is where the child Murugan is said to have explained the meaning of Om to his father Shiva, earning the name Swaminatha, teacher of his father. Sixty steps, one for each year of the cycle, lead up to the shrine.

temples.name: Sankat Mochan Hanuman Mandir
temples.about: Founded by the poet-saint Tulsidas, author of the Ramcharitmanas, Sankat Mochan, the remover of difficulties, faces Rama in the same temple. Tuesdays and Saturdays bring long queues, and the Sankat Mochan Sangeet Samaroh each April is one of India's great classical music festivals.

temples.name: Salasar Balaji Temple
temples.about: In Churu district, Salasar Balaji is Hanuman with a round, bearded and moustached face, an image said to have been found by a farmer while ploughing in 1754. Large fairs gather here at Chaitra and Ashvin Purnima.

temples.name: Hanuman Garhi
temples.about: Seventy-six steps climb to this fortress-like temple in Ayodhya, where Hanuman is said to keep watch over Rama's city. Pilgrims traditionally visit Hanuman Garhi before the Ram Janmabhoomi temple.

temples.name: Arulmigu Anjaneyar Temple
temples.about: An eighteen-foot Anjaneyar stands in the open, under the sky, facing Narasimha's cave temple across the way. Famous for the vadai malai, a garland of thousands of vadai, and the butter alankaram, it celebrates Hanumath Jayanthi in Margazhi.

temples.name: Sabarimala Sree Dharma Sastha Temple
temples.about: In the Periyar forests, Ayyappa, Dharma Sastha, sits in yogic posture on a hilltop reached by a forest climb. Pilgrims keep a 41-day vratham, wear black, and carry the irumudi up the eighteen holy steps, calling 'Swamiye Saranam Ayyappa'. The Mandala season and Makaravilakku draw millions.

temples.name: Aryankavu Sree Dharma Sastha Temple
temples.about: One of the five Sastha temples associated with Ayyappa's life, on the Kerala-Tamil Nadu border, Aryankavu worships Sastha as a young householder. The Thrikkalyanam festival in Dhanu, his celestial wedding, is kept with Saurashtra Brahmin custom.

temples.name: Shri Shaneshwar Devasthan
temples.about: Shani is worshipped here as a five-and-a-half-foot black stone in the open, without a roof. The village is famous for homes built without doors, a mark of its trust in Shani, and devotees pour oil over the stone, especially on Saturdays and Shani Amavasya.

temples.name: Sri Dharbaranyeswarar Temple
temples.about: In this Shiva temple near Karaikal, Shani Bhagavan has his own shrine, and it is the Navagraha temple for Saturn. Pilgrims bathe in the Nala Theertham, and the temple is busiest at Sani Peyarchi, when Saturn moves into a new sign.

temples.name: Pashupatinath Temple
temples.about: On the banks of the Bagmati, Pashupatinath is Shiva as Lord of all beings and the most sacred temple of Nepal. Its pagoda with gilded roofs and silver doors stands amid hundreds of shrines and ashrams, and on Maha Shivaratri sadhus and pilgrims from across Nepal and India fill its grounds. A UNESCO World Heritage site.

temples.name: Muktinath Temple
temples.about: High in the Mustang valley at about 3,700 metres, Muktinath is one of the 108 Divya Desams sung by the Alvars, sacred to Vishnu and also to Buddhists. Pilgrims bathe under its 108 water spouts and see the eternal flame burning over water at the nearby Jwala Mai shrine; the Kali Gandaki below gives the shaligram stones.

temples.name: Janaki Mandir
temples.about: Janakpur is held to be the city of King Janaka, where Sita was born and married Rama. The white marble Janaki Mandir, built in 1910 in Mughal and Rajput style, is the heart of Vivaha Panchami, when the wedding of Sita and Rama is celebrated, and of Ram Navami in the Mithila region.

temples.name: Sri Venkateswara Temple
temples.about: Consecrated in 1977, among the first traditional Hindu temples built in the United States, with sculptors brought from India and the design modelled on Tirumala. It is a place of pilgrimage for Hindus across North America, known for its Venkateswara kalyanam and its annual Brahmotsavam.

temples.name: Sri Maha Vallabha Ganapati Devasthanam
temples.about: The Hindu Temple Society of North America's Ganesha temple, consecrated in 1977, is one of the oldest traditional temples in the United States. Built in granite in the South Indian style, it is famous for its Ganesha Chaturthi festival and the canteen beneath it, which serves South Indian food to visitors.

temples.name: Malibu Hindu Temple (Sri Venkateswara Swamy)
temples.about: Set in the Santa Monica Mountains and consecrated in 1981, the temple of Sri Venkateswara is the oldest Hindu temple in Southern California. Built in the Chola and Pallava style, it draws devotees from across Los Angeles for its weekend abhishekam and its Brahmotsavam.

temples.name: Shiva-Vishnu Temple
temples.about: The Hindu Community and Cultural Center's temple joins North and South Indian architecture, with Shiva and Vishnu as the principal deities and shrines for many others. It serves the San Francisco Bay Area's Hindu community and is known for its Maha Shivaratri and Navaratri celebrations.

temples.name: Sri Venkateswara Temple (Balaji Mandir)
temples.about: One of the largest Hindu temples in the United States, dedicated to Lord Venkateswara with shrines to Padmavati, Andal and many others. It serves the large Hindu community of New Jersey and New York and is known for its Brahmotsavam and its daily kalyanotsavam.

temples.name: Sri Ganesha Temple
temples.about: Built in the Chola style with a tall rajagopuram, this temple of Ganesha is a landmark of the American South. It serves Hindu families across Tennessee and is known for its Ganesha Chaturthi and Vinayaka festivals.

temples.name: Kauai's Hindu Monastery (Iraivan Temple)
temples.about: A Shaiva monastery founded in 1970 beside the Wailua River, where the Kadavul temple holds a Nataraja in daily worship and the Iraivan Temple, carved by hand in white granite in India and assembled on the island, is dedicated to Shiva as a crystal lingam.

temples.name: Neem Karoli Baba Ashram and Hanuman Temple
temples.about: An ashram in memory of the saint Neem Karoli Baba, centred on a large murti of Hanuman lying in flight, brought from India in the 1970s. Visitors come for the daily arati, the singing of the Hanuman Chalisa and the meals served to all.

temples.name: Hindu Temple of Greater Chicago (Rama Temple)
temples.about: Consecrated in 1986, the temple on the hill at Lemont is dedicated to Rama with Sita, Lakshmana and Hanuman, beside a Ganesha-Shiva-Durga temple in the North Indian style. It serves the Hindu community of the Chicago area and is known for Ram Navami and Diwali.

temples.name: Durga Temple of Virginia
temples.about: A temple of Ma Durga serving the Washington DC area, with shrines to many deities. It is known for its Navaratri festival, when devotees gather each night for puja, garba and bhajans.

temples.name: Hindu Temple of Atlanta (Sri Venkateswara)
temples.about: A temple of Sri Venkateswara built in the South Indian style, with a Shiva temple beside it, serving the Hindu community of Georgia. It is known for its Brahmotsavam and its kalyanotsavam.

temples.name: Kali Mandir
temples.about: A small temple of Ma Kali in the hills of Laguna Beach, where worship follows the Bengali tradition of Dakshineswar. It is known for its Kali Puja and Durga Puja, open to all who come.
